blocks.text: Abbotsford: how mobile and manufactured homes work here
Local rules that affect park-home buyers

items.t: Zoning / OCP: Zoning Bylaw No. 2400 (2014) governs. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach / garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — Abbotsford's rules only. SSMUH does not apply to pad tenancies.
Three Abbotsford "Maplewoods" are three different tenures: A buyer searching the name alone will mix tenures.

A park's 55+ rule is not a strata bylaw: Occupancy, pets, rentals of the home and buyer approval in a pad park are set by the park's own rules and the tenancy agreement — which is why park listings can bar rentals of the homes outright, something no strata could do today. Get the specific park's current rules in writing.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Abbotsford's manufactured-home parks sit in the built-up west, central, and Poplar areas of the city, not on the Sumas or Matsqui Prairie floodplains to the east and north. The City's flood response page describes Sumas Prairie as a 90-square-kilometre low-lying area in East Abbotsford, which is a different part of the city from the named parks below.

A second, different form exists on ordinary city streets: the Infill Manufactured Home Zone (RSMH) covers fee-simple manufactured homes on individual urban lots, with a minimum interior lot size of 495 square metres.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: the housing stock

items.t: Abbotsford offers three distinct forms: rented pads in RH1 parks, a bare-land strata community, and fee-simple manufactured homes on RSMH lots.

Paradise Park, 31313 Livingstone Avenue in Abbotsford West, is a pad-rental park; City public hearing records list the address with RH1 zoning, and 2010 hearing minutes record Paradise Park residents at units in 31313 Livingstone Avenue, with one resident stating the park is for residents 55 years and older.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The City's updated Official Community Plan, Abbotsforward 2050, approved at the end of 2025, creates new opportunities for non-market housing on land designated Urban Area Manufactured Home Park, which signals the City treats park land as a housing resource rather than only a redevelopment reserve.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Allwood park precedent shows redevelopment is not theoretical here: 2800 Allwood Street was rezoned from Mobile Home Park (RH1) to a Comprehensive Development zone for townhouses, recorded in 2013 Council minutes.
Policy 400-3-07 expressly did not apply to Areas 2, 3, and 4 of the Allwood park, a carve-out a buyer would only find by reading the adopted policy text.

Council approved a 4 percent water increase and a 4 percent sewer increase in January 2026, effective March 1, 2026, which flows into park operating costs and, through the provincial formula, into allowable pad-rent pass-throughs.
A new Highstreet transit exchange with five bus bays opened September 6, 2026 near Highstreet Shopping Centre, an 8.1-million-dollar project that anchors Abbotsford's bus network in the west end.
The City's Climate Resilience Strategy names Sumas Prairie, Matsqui Prairie, and Clayburn Village as particularly flood-vulnerable neighbourhoods — the park neighbourhoods are not on that list.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: costs and taxes

items.t: From March 1, 2026, residential water is billed at 1.46 dollars per cubic metre and sewer at 1.35 dollars per cubic metre; utility bills are issued bi-monthly and a 5 percent discount applies if the bill is paid by its due date.
Pad-rent increases are percentages only: the 2026 provincial limit is 2.3 percent plus the proportionate share of increases in local government levies and regulated utility fees.

British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) runs Abbotsford's buses through the Central Fraser Valley system, which also serves Mission; its January 4, 2026 expansion covered Route 1 Highstreet/University of the Fraser Valley (UFV), Route 2 Highstreet/McMillan, Route 21 Aldergrove/Abbotsford, Route 31 Abbotsford/Mission, and Route 66 Fraser Valley Express.
A single bus ride in the Central Fraser Valley cost 2.75 dollars from September 6, 2026, the same day the new Highstreet Mall Exchange reopened.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Mobile Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is the city's defining risk, but it is location-specific: the City's flood page records major floods in 1990, 2021, and December 2025, when 485 properties were under Evacuation Order and Highway 1 closed for three days — impacts centred on the prairie lowlands, not the urban park districts.
The Allwood rezoning shows an RH1 park can be rezoned to another use through a public process, so a buyer should search the City's development planning records for the park's address before buying.

faq.a: The figure that governs is the specific site's tenancy agreement — confirm the current pad rent, what it includes, and its increase history with the park for the exact site before offering.
faq.q: What pad rent should I expect in an Abbotsford park?

faq.a: It is the home's certification decal — Z-240 series for mobile homes, A-277 series for modular homes, with a unique identifier usually near the front door or on the electrical panel. The Province states a manufactured home may not be sold unless the original legible CSA decal is attached; if it is lost, the home must be re-certified through Technical Safety BC's electrical inspection and approval-label route before it can be listed for sale.
faq.q: Why does the CSA label matter?

faq.q: Does Abbotsford have a manufactured home park redevelopment policy?

faq.a: At Paradise Park you rent the pad and own only the home, under a Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act tenancy that needs the park owner's consent to assign. At Downes Road Estates you buy a bare-land strata lot as well as the home, so title is registered land ownership, strata bylaws and fees apply, and there is no pad tenancy to assign.
faq.q: What is the difference between a pad at Paradise Park and a lot at Downes Road Estates?

faq.a: The named parks are not in Sumas Prairie, but do not assume any address is flood-free.

faq.a: For 2026 the limit for a manufactured home site is 2.3 percent plus the proportionate increase in local government levies and regulated utility fees on the park's common property, with three full months' notice and only one increase in any 12 months.

faq.q: Is there an official median price for Abbotsford manufactured homes?

faq.a: On a rented pad, the buyer purchases the manufactured home itself and holds a manufactured home site tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, paying monthly site rent to the park; on owned land (freehold or bare-land strata), the buyer also acquires the land interest, which transfers through the Land Title Office. In both cases, in B.C. the sale of the manufactured home is only effective if the transaction is registered in the Manufactured Home Registry.
faq.q: What is the difference between a pad-rental park home and a manufactured home on owned land?

faq.a: Once every 12 months, on at least 3 full months' notice, and no more than the yearly limit set by the Residential Tenancy Branch: for manufactured home site tenancies the 2026 limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees, and the 2027 limit is 2.2% plus the proportional amount.
